original_statement:
Request: MOTIVATION (concrete leak, exophial 2026-07-24):
exophial's acceptance probes scripts/check_dispatch_gate_preserve_reason.py and scripts/check_dispatch_worker_exit_reason.py start a REAL exophiald reducer on the HOST — via run_cli_dispatch(repo, pebble_id, ...) inside a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() — instead of the container e2e harness the project already has (the exophial-e2e-* images that run the reducer in an isolated container and reap it on container exit). When the owning session died, one such probe orphaned: a host reducer holding a host .exophial/exophiald.lock plus a poller stuck in a sleep loop, reparented to systemd --user, running ~37h with no reaper, leaving an uncleaned /tmp temp repo. The probe's timeout 60 wrapper could not kill it (no -k / SIGTERM ignored). Root enabler: a real reducer run bare on the host rather than in a container.

WHAT TO BUILD:
A structural (AST) rule, in aspergillus's normal generic-rule + consumer-config shape (like the ASP-FSM rules), that REJECTS at the commit boundary any file under a configured path set (exophial: tests/**, scripts/**) that REACHES a reducer/daemon-start symbol WITHOUT going through the sanctioned container fixture. Reducer-start symbol set (consumer-configured; exophial's values): run_cli_dispatch; exophial.daemon.start / daemon.start; Dispatcher(...).run / dispatcher.run; and subprocess.run / Popen whose argv contains 'exophial dispatch' | 'exophiald' | 'exophial start'. Exemption: the call is inside / obtained from the container e2e fixture (a configured marker — a decorator like @requires_container_reducer, or use of the known container-harness fixture/module under tests/e2e). A file that starts a reducer only through the container harness passes; one that starts it bare fails.

WHY THIS LAYER (not a runtime guard):
Enforcement must reject at a boundary, not check at runtime. A runtime 'if PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST: raise' in daemon.start is (a) test logic in the PRODUCTION reducer path — the dev/prod-coupling antipattern — and (b) bypassable (subprocess the CLI, or construct Dispatcher directly), so it is a tripwire, not enforcement. A pre-commit AST rule stays entirely in the lint layer, touches NO production code, and has teeth: exophial re-runs the same commit-boundary gate at merge, so a red result means the integrator PRESERVEs and never merges — the bad pattern is unmergeable, the same way block_worktree_leak.py and the ASP-FSM rules are enforced.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A fixture test file under tests/ that calls run_cli_dispatch (or spawns 'exophial dispatch', or daemon.start, or Dispatcher(...).run) with NO container-fixture marker is REJECTED (rule fires, non-zero).
- The same call routed through the container fixture / carrying the exemption marker PASSES.
- A file OUTSIDE the configured path set (e.g. src/exophial/daemon.py itself — the legitimate production start) is NOT flagged: the rule is scoped to test/script paths only, so production reducer start is untouched.
- Rule is generic + consumer-configured (path globs, symbol set, exemption marker in exophial's aspergillus config), not exophial-hardcoded.

HONEST LIMIT: static reachability has the usual holes (dynamic dispatch, string-built argv). Acceptable — these probes write the call straightforwardly; the rule catches honest code, which is the regression vector. exophial wires it into its own .pre-commit-config.yaml.

NOTE (appended):
exophial-authoring:
restatement: Add a new structural (AST-based) pre-commit rule to aspergillus, built in the same generic-rule-plus-consumer-config shape the request models on the ASP-FSM rules — the closest existing template in this repo is ASP410 (InProcessE2E), which already has the path-glob + symbol-set + exemption shape via subclass-overridden class attributes (aspergillus's rules are configured per-consumer by subclassing, not by an external config file; the request's own comparison to block_worktree_leak.py points at a runtime hook in the sibling exophial repo, not an aspergillus AST rule, so that specific precedent doesn't transfer, but the pattern it's gesturing at — a commit-boundary gate with teeth — does) — so that a real reducer/daemon process can never be started, bare, on the host from inside a test or script file again. Concretely: for any file that falls under a consumer-configured set of path globs (for exophial: tests/** and scripts/**), the rule performs a static check for a consumer-configured set of reducer/daemon-start symbols (for exophial: run_cli_dispatch; exophial.daemon.start / daemon.start; Dispatcher(...).run / dispatcher.run; and subprocess.run / Popen calls whose argv contains 'exophial dispatch', 'exophiald', or 'exophial start'). If that file reaches one of those symbols without passing through a consumer-configured exemption marker (for exophial: a decorator such as @requires_container_reducer, or use of the known container e2e harness fixture/module under tests/e2e), the rule rejects the commit (non-zero result). If the same call is routed through the exemption marker, the rule passes it. Files outside the configured path globs — including the legitimate production reducer-start code itself — are never flagged, no matter what symbols they contain, because the rule's scope is limited to the configured test/script paths. All of the exophial-specific values (path globs, symbol set, exemption marker) must live in a per-consumer configuration (following aspergillus's existing subclass-override pattern), not be hardcoded into the generic rule engine itself, so other consumer repos can reuse it with their own values. This closes the concrete leak: on 2026-07-24 one of exophial's acceptance probes started a real exophiald reducer bare on the host (via run_cli_dispatch in a temp directory) instead of through the container e2e harness; when its owning session died, the reducer orphaned for ~37 hours holding a host lock, with no reaper and an uncleaned temp repo, because enforcement lived only as a bypassable runtime tripwire rather than a commit-boundary gate.

A fixture test file under tests/ that calls run_cli_dispatch (or spawns 'exophial dispatch', or daemon.start, or Dispatcher(...).run) with NO container-fixture marker is REJECTED (rule fires, non-zero).
The same call routed through the container fixture / carrying the exemption marker PASSES.

A file OUTSIDE the configured path set (e.g. src/exophial/daemon.py itself — the legitimate production start) is NOT flagged: the rule is scoped to test/script paths only, so production reducer start is untouched.

goal: Give aspergillus a generic, consumer-configured AST rule that rejects, at the commit boundary, any test/script file that reaches a reducer/daemon-start call without going through the sanctioned container fixture — so the class of bug that let exophial orphan a bare host reducer for ~37 hours can't be committed again.
acceptance_criteria: Point the check at a completely different, made-up configuration (a different watched folder and a different symbol name, unrelated to exophial) and an unguarded call to that made-up symbol inside that made-up folder. The check should still catch it and fail, showing its rules come entirely from the configuration handed to it rather than from exophial-specific logic baked into the tool.

Run the check against a test file that starts the reducer directly (calling run_cli_dispatch, spawning 'exophial dispatch', calling daemon.start, or calling Dispatcher(...).run) with no container-fixture marker anywhere. The check should fail (report a non-zero result).

Run the check against the same kind of reducer-starting call, this time written so it goes through the sanctioned container fixture (carries the exemption marker). The check should pass (report a zero result).

Run the check against a file located outside the configured test/script folders (standing in for the real production reducer-start code), even though it contains the same reducer-start call. The check should pass (report a zero result) because that file is out of scope.
